correctness.rationale: For fixed n>=3 and alpha>0, the tangent polygon is bounded iff every Dirichlet angular gap Yi<1/2; area=perimeter/2=sum_i tan(pi Yi). The beta density at 1/2 is positive finite, giving each large tangent gap probability ~f(1/2)/(pi t). Integrating the Dirichlet corners proves two simultaneously large gaps are o(t^-1), and a one-big-gap squeeze yields P(A>t|bounded)~c/t, c=n*2^(2-n alpha)/(pi Beta(alpha,(n-1)alpha)*p), p=1-n Pr(Y1>=1/2). Thus E[A^r|bounded]<infinity iff r<1. Independently recomputed beta edge masses and constants for n=3,4,5 and several alpha; at n=3 alpha=1 the coefficient equals 12/pi. Finite checks support but do not replace the asymptotic corner/squeeze proof.

Fixed-size Dirichlet angular gaps, including iid uniform tangencies, make the explicit first-order Pareto coefficient and infinite conditional mean mathematically significant; they distinguish rare near-semicircle singularity from the separate large-number-of-sides Gaussian approximation regime.
